descriptions: Constant Naming Rules
1. The identifier must always start with an uppercase letter (A-Z).
2. Only uppercase letters, digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
3. Words are separated using a single underscore (_).
4. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
5. The identifier must not start or end with an underscore.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be an uppercase letter or a digit.
7. Only uppercase letters are allowed (no lowercase characters).
Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with a lowercase letter.
2. Words are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character of the identifier.
4. The underscore (_) is not allowed anywhere in the name.
5. A name that needs a semantic separator is a structured variable and answers to structured_variable instead.
6. Only letters (A-Z, a-z) and digits (0-9) are allowed.
Structured Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier follows the variable rules, with one underscore (_) allowed as a semantic separator.
2. The identifier must start with a lowercase letter.
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character of the identifier.
5. Exactly one underscore is allowed, and it may be anywhere except as the first or the last character.
6. After the underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed, and neither is a second separator elsewhere in the name.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Command Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix cmd.
2. The prefix is followed by one to three digits, leading zeros included: cmd0, cmd00, cmd000 and cmd999 are all accepted.
3. The digits may be followed by a single lowercase letter, which is optional.
4. A single underscore (_) always follows, and it is the only one in the name.
5. After the underscore the name follows the variable rules: it starts with a lowercase letter and continues in camelCase, with digits allowed anywhere but that first character.
6. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9) and that one underscore are allowed.
7. It belongs to the Input of object_container_for_sequences and nowhere else, which is where a sequence takes the commands that drive it.
Waiting Point Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix wp.
2. The prefix is followed by one to three digits, leading zeros included: wp0, wp00, wp000 and wp999 are all accepted.
3. The digits may be followed by a single lowercase letter, which is optional.
4. A single underscore (_) always follows, and it is the only one in the name.
5. After the underscore the name follows the variable rules: it starts with a lowercase letter and continues in camelCase, with digits allowed anywhere but that first character.
6. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9) and that one underscore are allowed.

7. It belongs to the Output of object_container_for_sequences and nowhere else, which is where a sequence says which waiting point it has reached. It is command_variable with wp where that one has cmd.
Sequence Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with an uppercase S.
2. The S is followed by exactly three digits (000-999): the step number.
3. The digits are followed by a single underscore (_).
4. The name after that underscore must start with an uppercase letter and continue in camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each semantic separator, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Transition Variable Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix t_.
2. The prefix is followed by exactly three digits (000-999): the step the transition leaves.
3. The digits are followed by a single underscore (_).
4. The identifier ends with either three more digits (000-999), the step the transition enters, or the literal nop when it enters none.
5. Nothing else is allowed: the whole name is the prefix, two segments and the separators between them.
Interruption Parameter Naming Rules

TIA Portal writes these into an OB's Input itself and nobody can rename them, so no naming convention of yours applies to them: Initial_Call, true on the first call after a restart, and Remanence, true when retentive data was kept.

Every name inside a block is checked, TIA's own included, so this rule is what lets them pass. It belongs to the Input of interruption and nowhere else: an OB's Temp and Constant are the engineer's, and answer to variable and constant.
1. The name must be one of the list, spelled exactly as TIA spells it.
2. The pattern is closed at both ends, so it accepts those two names and nothing that merely starts with one of them.

3. When an OB type brings a parameter this does not name yet - a hardware interrupt's LADDR and USI, a time error's Fault_ID - add it to the list rather than loosening the pattern. The report names the member that failed, which is where you will see it first.
Graph Parameter Naming Rules
TIA Portal writes these into a GRAPH block's interface itself and nobody can rename them: INIT_SQ and ACK_EF in Input, S_NO, S_MORE and S_ACTIVE in Output, and RT_DATA in Static.

Every name inside a block is checked, TIA's own included, so this rule is what lets them pass. It belongs to the Input, Output and Static of object_container_for_sequences, which is where a sequence written in GRAPH lands.
1. The name must be one of the list, spelled exactly as TIA spells it.
2. The pattern is closed at both ends, so RT_DATABASE and S_NOTHING are not accepted by it.
3. Enabling another GRAPH option adds more of them - OFF_SQ, HALT_SQ, S_PREV, S_NEXT and the rest - and each is added to this list the first time a report names it.

4. The steps and the transitions are deliberately not in it: TIA writes those members, but the engineer names them in the GRAPH editor, so they answer to sequence_variable and transition_variable like the rules they are.
5. A GRAPH block's Base section, and what lives inside RT_DATA, are the interface of a Siemens type rather than of the block, and are never checked at all.
Interrupt Naming Rules
1. Every interrupt name must start with an uppercase letter (A-Z).
2. Words are separated using an underscore (_).
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed.
4. Only uppercase letters, digits, and underscores are allowed.
5. The interrupt name must not end with an underscore.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be an uppercase letter or a digit.
Data Container Naming Rules
1. Every interrupt name must start with an uppercase letter (A-Z).
2. Words are separated using an underscore (_).
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed.
4. Only uppercase letters, digits, and underscores are allowed.
5. The interrupt name must not end with an underscore.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be an uppercase letter or a digit.

3. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character of the identifier.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
5. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
6. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
7. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Safety Data Type Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix F_.
2. The first character after F_ must be a lowercase letter.
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the F_ prefix.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Unsafety Data Type Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix UF_. It is the safety rule with UF where that one has F.
2. The first character after UF_ must be a lowercase letter.
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the UF_ prefix.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Enumeration Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix E.
2. The first character after E must be an uppercase letter (A-Z).
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the E prefix.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Function Naming Rules
1. Every function name must start with a single underscore (_) followed by a lowercase letter.
2. A double underscore marks a private function, which is a rule of its own: see private_function.
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the function name.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
5. Words within a segment must follow lower camel case:
5.1. The first word starts with a lowercase letter.
5.2. Each subsequent word starts with an uppercase letter.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7. Consecutive semantic separators are not allowed, except for the leading __ used to indicate a private function.
8. The function name must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Safety Function Naming Rules
1. Every safety function must start with _F_.
2. The first character after the prefix must be a lowercase letter.
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the function name.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
4.1. Words within a segment must follow lower camel case:
4.2. The first word starts with a lowercase letter.
5. Each subsequent word starts with an uppercase letter.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7.Consecutive semantic separators are not allowed, except in the prefixes __F_.
8. The function name must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Private Function Naming Rules
1. Every private function name must start with a double underscore (__) followed by a lowercase letter.
2. Everything after the prefix follows the same rules as a function.
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the name.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
5. Words within a segment must follow lower camel case: the first word starts lowercase, each subsequent word starts uppercase.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7. The name must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Private Safety Function Naming Rules
1. Every private safety function must start with __F_.
2. The first character after the prefix must be a lowercase letter.
3. Everything after the prefix follows the same rules as a safety function.
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the name.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7. The name must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Unsafety Function Naming Rules
1. Every unsafety function must start with _UF_. It is the safety rule with UF where that one has F.
2. The first character after the prefix must be a lowercase letter.
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the name.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
5. Words within a segment must follow lower camel case: the first word starts lowercase, each subsequent word starts uppercase.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7. The name must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Private Unsafety Function Naming Rules
1. Every private unsafety function must start with __UF_.
2. The first character after the prefix must be a lowercase letter.
3. Everything after the prefix follows the same rules as an unsafety function.
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed within the name.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After a semantic separator (_), the next segment must start with a lowercase letter.
7. The name must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Subroutine Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with an uppercase letter (A-Z).
2. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character of the identifier.
4. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
5. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
6. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
7. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Safety Subroutine Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix F_.
2. The first character after F_ must be an uppercase letter (A-Z).
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the F_ prefix.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Unsafety Subroutine Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix UF_. It is the safety rule with UF where that one has F.
2. The first character after UF_ must be an uppercase letter (A-Z).
3. Words within a segment are separated using camelCase (the first letter of each subsequent word is uppercase).
4. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the UF_ prefix.
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each underscore, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Object Container Naming Rules
1. The identifier must always start with the prefix _oc_.
2. The first character after _oc_ must be a lowercase letter.
3. Digits (0-9) are allowed anywhere except as the first character after the _oc_ prefix.
4. Words within a segment follow lower camel case (the first word starts lowercase, each subsequent word starts uppercase).
5. The underscore (_) may be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
6. After each _, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
7. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed, except within the fixed prefix _oc_.
8. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
9. Only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_) are allowed.
Object Container for Sequences Naming Rules
1. The identifier must start with the prefix _oc_seq.
2. After _oc_seq, it must contain 1 to 3 digits (0-9).
3. The digits must be immediately followed by an underscore (_).
4. After the underscore, the rest of the name follows the same rules as Object Container naming rules:
4.1. Lower camel case within segments.
4.2. Words separated by camelCase (uppercase letter for each new word).
4.3. _ can be used as a semantic separator between logical segments.
4.4. After each _, the next character must be a lowercase letter or a digit.
5. Digits are allowed anywhere except at the start of the post-prefix name segment.
6. Consecutive underscores (__) are not allowed (except inside the fixed prefix structure).
7. The identifier must not end with an underscore.
8. Only letters, digits, and underscores are allowed.
